# Tech Destination Sri Lanka

> Tech Destination Sri Lanka helps companies abroad hire technology talent, find software outsourcing partners and set up teams in Sri Lanka. It publishes independent, sourced reporting on the software, products and companies built by Sri Lankan technology talent.

Sri Lanka is UTC+5:30. Colombo is the main technology hub. Every story lists its sources at the end.

## Key facts
- How big are Sri Lanka's IT and BPM exports? USD 1.645 billion in 2025, up 8.8% on the year, according to the Export Development Board. The Central Bank's narrower balance of payments measure records about USD 0.8 billion, and the industry estimates about USD 2 billion, because revenue booked abroad and freelance income are not fully captured.
- How many people work in tech in Sri Lanka? The Export Development Board cites 146,000 people employed in the sector. Press reports of industry estimates in 2026 put it at about 175,000. The last full official survey counted 124,873 ICT workers in 2018.
- How many ICT graduates does Sri Lanka produce each year? Startup Genome's 2026 report says 12,000+. Industry estimates reported in the press in 2026 say about 17,000 enter the sector each year.
- How does Sri Lanka rank for tech talent? Third in Asia for affordable tech talent in Startup Genome's Global Startup Ecosystem Report 2026, which also recorded Sri Lanka climbing more than 65 places in its emerging ecosystem rankings, the biggest jump that year.
- What are the biggest Sri Lankan tech exits? Virtusa, cofounded by a Sri Lankan, was acquired for USD 2 billion in 2021. WSO2 was acquired by EQT for USD 600 million in 2024. The London Stock Exchange bought MillenniumIT after choosing its trading platform. JPMorganChase acquired WealthOS in 2026.
- Which global companies run R&D in Sri Lanka? IFS runs 75% of its global R&D from Colombo. Sysco, Synopsys and Zebra Technologies run engineering or R&D centres there. HCLTech, EY, HSBC and WNS run delivery operations.
- Who are the largest tech employers in Sri Lanka? Virtusa has 3,000+ engineers in Colombo and IFS has 2,200+ employees there.
- What time zone is Sri Lanka in? UTC+5:30 all year, with no daylight saving. That is 1.5 hours ahead of the UAE, 3.5 to 4.5 hours ahead of Central Europe, 4.5 to 5.5 hours ahead of the UK and 9.5 to 10.5 hours ahead of US Eastern time.
- What does a software engineer earn in Sri Lanka? A median of about LKR 177,000 a month (about USD 535) according to self reported Glassdoor data for 2026, and about LKR 260,000 for a senior engineer. Export focused employers pay more.
- What tax do IT exporters pay in Sri Lanka? 15% on income from services exported and paid for in foreign currency, from 1 April 2025. The standard corporate rate is 30%.
- Can foreigners fully own a tech company in Sri Lanka? Yes. IT and software companies can be 100% foreign owned and can repatriate profits, according to the Board of Investment.
- Which universities feed the tech industry? The University of Moratuwa, a top contributor to Google Summer of Code since 2004, and SLIIT, the largest private tech university with 25,000+ students, are the best known. Peradeniya and Ruhuna teach chip design with a curriculum built with Synopsys.
- Where are the main tech parks in Colombo? Orion City in Colombo 09 houses 85+ technology companies. TRACE Expert City in Colombo 10, the World Trade Center in Colombo 01 and Port City Colombo are the other main hubs.
- Is there an AI industry in Sri Lanka? Yes. Roar Global runs the country's first AI gateway, Xeynergy builds its own AI products and Rootcode builds AI platforms for the Estonian government.

- [Why Sri Lanka for AI companies](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/why-sri-lanka/ai/): Sri Lankan companies build AI gateways, agentic developer tools and national AI infrastructure for Estonia. The evidence, the roles and how to hire.

- [Why Sri Lanka for semiconductor and embedded software companies](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/why-sri-lanka/semiconductors-embedded/): Synopsys engineers chip design software in Colombo and Zebra runs device software R&D here. The evidence, the roles and how to hire embedded talent in Sri Lanka.
- [Why Sri Lanka for logistics, supply chain and travel tech companies](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/why-sri-lanka/logistics-travel/): A travel platform with a billion bookings, warehouse automation and Sysco's supply chain systems are built by Sri Lankan engineers. How to hire them.
- [Why Sri Lanka for govtech and public sector technology](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/why-sri-lanka/govtech/): Sri Lankan companies build AI infrastructure for Estonia, public sector software for Sweden and a transformation programme for Qatar. The evidence and how to hire.

- [A Colombo team built Sri Lanka's first AI gateway, with 200+ models billed in rupees. Meet Roar Global](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/stories/roar-global/): Roar started as a digital publisher in 2014. It is now an AI led venture builder with 150+ specialists and no outside capital.
- [Six engineers with no funding and no office built an 80 person AI software company. Meet Xeynergy](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/stories/xeynergy/): Bootstrapped in 2021, Xeynergy now earns multi million dollar recurring revenue and ships its own AI products.
- [A publicly listed Swedish tech company calls its Colombo office its global tech center. Meet Frontwalker](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/stories/frontwalker/): Frontwalker Group has built enterprise and public sector software for 35+ years. Its 100+ engineers in Sri Lanka carry delivery for the whole group.
